details:
Currently, you can't favorite worlds unless they're fully public (submitted to labs or approved by labs).

You can press the favorite button and it'll even ask you what category to save it to, but it just won't actually work. This sometimes results in some people thinking they favorited the world when they really didn't.

This is pointless though because one can just view the world on the website and save it as a browser favorite or whatever.

So I propose you either allow people to favorite worlds that aren't published, or you strip the ability to visit unpublished worlds without the presence of the world author (in the same way that you prevent people from joining Friends+ unless they have a friend there) and the ability for anyone but the author to view it on the website.

I'm in favor of the former because I don't really see why there's any attempt to prevent people from accessing unpublished worlds as the only way the world ever gets out in the first place is if the creator has been showing it around and in that case I feel that the responsibility for any spreading of the world from that point befalls them and their friends, and the author can always delete or upload to a new ID if they want to, so I don't think this is something that VRC needs to bother with policing on any technical level.

However if what you want to do is prevent people from accessing unpublished worlds for whatever reason, then you should do a better job of it. It shouldn't be possible for anyone but the world owner to open the world on the website, the "favorite" and "view on website" buttons should either be grayed-out with or removed as to make it clear that the world is not public and as such is not favoritable or accessible on the website.

I say this because the current implementation is about the least sensible possible. You can't really favorite worlds yet the UI implies that you can, and it's a pointless restriction because you can just bypass the issue by viewing the world on the website. So the result is just confusing for people with no benefit. It's none of my business which way you go with things, but whichever you choose just do it right and don't settle on half-measures (you'll find this sentiment in a lot of the things I propose).

So yeah, I'm just saying that I think it'd be best for you to commit to either one mindset or the other and execute that properly, rather than this awkward in-between state that would be unclear to newer people or people that don't pay close enough attention.

Thanks.
title: Either allow favoriting of unpublished worlds, or disallow it in a more proper manner than currently implemented.
